fixes.explanation: The song never talks about the size of the harvest, friend. It says he waited for good grapes, "…but the fruit it produced was sour!" The problem is the taste, not the amount. Picture me pulling out a full tray, golden and gorgeous, and the first bite is pure salt. Nobody at that table is asking how many cookies there are, baker.

Idol worship isn't what this verse says, friend. It says, "He looked for justice, but saw bloodshed…" Notice how this lands on people hurting people, not just on something people bowed down to. I think that's why the next line is about a cry of distress: "…for righteousness, but heard a cry of distress."

Laziness isn't in this verse, baker. The text says, "He looked for justice, but saw bloodshed…" Nobody here is accused of napping on the job. The next line says He looked for righteousness, "…but heard a cry of distress," so I think the song is about people getting hurt, not people slacking.
